A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRADEO work. Their complete main texts and Appendices A-E are readable, allowing reliable matching of equations, tables, figures, and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-correlation measurements, pairwise preference accuracy, ablations, and evaluations of eight video-generation models in Sections 4-5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports per-dimension Qwen2-VL-7B baseline results in Table 2.

M1.justification: Both retain the same Qwen2-VL-7B-based evaluator, LoRA fine-tuning, four-stage reasoning pipeline, and Equation 1 objective. No algorithmic component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: The seven evaluation dimensions, GRADEO-Instruct, GRADEO-BENCH, T2VQA-DB, GenAI-Bench-Video, and TVGE coverage are unchanged. The expanded safety discussion introduces no new evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen2-VL-7B to the actual Table 2 comparison, although the base model already appeared in v1's aggregate ablation. Table 3's comparator set is unchanged. The newly cited Evaluation Agent is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Both retain the 340-sample test set, 1,600-video pairwise evaluation, evaluation metrics, 700-prompt benchmark, and training and generation settings. The added Table 2 baseline uses the existing comparison protocol.

E4.justification: The reasoning-step, fine-tuning, and CNN ablations are unchanged, with v1 Table 5 becoming v2 Table 4. The rationality case in v2 Figure 5 is the identical example from v1 Appendix C.2/Figure 12; its relocation adds no analysis evidence.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Human-annotation counts and agreement requirements are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds seven Qwen2-VL-7B result triplets, including quality SROCC/PLCC/MAE of 0.590/0.424/0.649. Existing numerical results, including the pairwise, ablation, and generator-benchmark tables, are unchanged. Section 5.3 also newly asserts an association between stronger instruction following and unsafe outputs, without new quantitative results.

T1.justification: The training objective and optical-flow/SSIM filtering formulas in Equations 1-3 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: the instruction dataset, interpretable reasoning-based evaluator, stronger alignment with human assessment, and benchmarking of generation models.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly explains rationality failures through prompt-induced hallucinations. Section 5.3 links unsafe generation to stronger prompt adherence and insufficient safety constraints, while the Impact Statement adds detection and safety-design recommendations. Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's promise that models, datasets, and code will be released soon, while retaining the dataset-release plan in Section 3. Implementation and reproducibility details in the appendices are unchanged. This changes release information, without establishing any actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Evaluation Agent and positions it as having fairness concerns across models and lacking human annotations. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic metadata or citation lettering rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 integrates the appendix qualitative example into the main narrative, expands selected discussion passages, adds acknowledgements, and makes small terminology and conference-header corrections. Most prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The rationality example moves from v1 Figure 12 to v2 Figure 5 with an explanatory caption; Figure 4's caption now identifies creativity. Table 2 gains a baseline row, and surrounding tables and appendix material are locally reflowed. Existing visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: The added per-dimension base-model results in Table 2 make the existing fine-tuning comparison more informative, while the relocated rationality example and clearer captions improve accessibility. These provide a modest gain rather than a substantial scientific advance. The new safety interpretation extends beyond the unchanged experimental controls, limiting its evidential value.
